questions.skill: Who-does-what puzzle
questions.stem:
Amir, Bella and Cody each play a different instrument (piano, drums or violin) and each has a different favourite colour (red, blue or green).
• The drummer's favourite colour is green.
• Bella does not play the piano.
• Cody's favourite colour is red.
• Amir plays the violin.
What is Bella's favourite colour?
questions.explanation: Amir plays violin, and Bella doesn't play piano, so Bella plays drums and Cody plays piano. The drummer likes green, so Bella's favourite colour is green.

distractors.B: blue is Amir's colour

questions.skill: Strengthen: a reason that makes the conclusion more likely
questions.stem:
Mia says: 'Our school should plant more trees around the playground. The shade will mean students can play outside more on hot days.'
Which statement, if true, most strengthens Mia's argument?

options.A: Many students prefer to play inside at lunchtime.
options.B: On days above 35 °C, students must stay indoors unless there is shade to play in.
options.C: Trees take several years to grow tall enough to give shade.
options.D: The school already has a large covered area next to the canteen.

questions.explanation: Mia's reason is that shade lets students play outside on hot days. If students are kept inside on very hot days unless there is shade, more shade directly means more outdoor play.

distractors.A: if anything this weakens it: fewer students would use the shade
distractors.C: this weakens the argument (the benefit is slow)
distractors.D: this weakens it: there may already be enough shade

questions.skill: Ordering from clues
questions.stem:
Five friends ran a race. There were no ties.
• Ana finished before Ben but after Cleo.
• Dev finished last.
• Eli finished straight after Ben.
Who came second?
questions.explanation: Dev is 5th. Eli is straight after Ben, so Ben can be 3rd at the latest (Eli 4th). Cleo and Ana are both before Ben, so the order is Cleo, Ana, Ben, Eli, Dev. Ana is second.

distractors.B: Ben is 3rd
distractors.D: Eli is 4th

questions.skill: Letter-shift code
questions.stem:
In a code, each letter is replaced by the letter two places later in the alphabet. After Z the alphabet starts again, so Y becomes A and Z becomes B.
What is the code for ZEBRA?
questions.explanation: Z → B, E → G, B → D, R → T, A → C: BGDTC.

distractors.A: moved two places back instead of forward
distractors.D: moved one place instead of two

questions.skill: Repeating timetable
questions.stem: A ferry leaves the wharf every 40 minutes, starting at 6:20 am. Kim arrives at the wharf at 9:05 am. How long does she wait for the next ferry?
questions.explanation: Ferries leave at 6:20, 7:00, 7:40, 8:20, 9:00, 9:40… Kim just misses the 9:00 ferry, so she waits from 9:05 to 9:40: 35 minutes.

distractors.B: counted 20-minute gaps
distractors.D: thought she has to wait a full gap

questions.skill: Spot the mistake: a result can have more than one cause
questions.stem:
Isla says: 'The library is closed on Mondays. The library is closed today, so today must be Monday.'
Which statement shows the mistake Isla has made?

options.A: The library might also be closed on days other than Monday.
options.B: The library might stay open late on some days.
options.C: Isla might have forgotten what day it is.
options.D: Isla does not go to the library very often.

questions.explanation: Knowing the library is closed every Monday doesn't mean Monday is the only day it closes. It might be a public holiday, for example.

distractors.B: opening late doesn't explain a closure
distractors.C: not a mistake in her reasoning
distractors.D: irrelevant to the logic

questions.stem:
Lily is taller than Mo but shorter than Nia. Ollie is taller than Nia. Pat is shorter than Mo.
Who is the third tallest?
questions.explanation: Tallest to shortest: Ollie, Nia, Lily, Mo, Pat. The third tallest is Lily.

distractors.B: Nia is 2nd
distractors.D: Ollie is the tallest

questions.skill: Whose reasoning: "only if" rules
questions.stem:
Information: At Hilltop School, students can join the chess club only if they are in Year 5 or Year 6. Every member of the chess club must attend Friday practice.

Kira: 'Josh goes to Friday practice, so he must be in the chess club.'
Ravi: 'Ella is in Year 4, so she cannot be in the chess club.'

If the information is true, whose reasoning is correct?
questions.explanation: Ravi is right: you can only join if you are in Year 5 or 6, so a Year 4 student cannot be a member. Kira is wrong: members must go to Friday practice, but nothing says only members go.

distractors.D: Ravi's reasoning does follow from the 'only if' rule

questions.skill: Strengthen: link the cause to the result
questions.stem:
The council claims that a new bike path along the river will reduce traffic jams on Main Road at peak hour.
Which statement, if true, most strengthens the council's claim?

options.A: Bike riding is good exercise for people of all ages.
options.B: The bike path will cost less to build than widening Main Road.
options.C: Many people who drive on Main Road at peak hour are travelling to places the bike path will connect.
options.D: Some people already ride their bikes on the footpath beside Main Road.

questions.explanation: To reduce traffic jams, some drivers must swap their car for the bike path. That is only likely if the path goes where those drivers are going.

distractors.A: true, but says nothing about traffic
distractors.B: about cost, not whether traffic will fall
distractors.D: these riders aren't in cars, so moving them won't reduce traffic

questions.skill: Symbols standing for numbers
questions.stem:
Each shape stands for a different number.
★ + ★ = ▲
▲ + ★ = 12
What is ▲ − ★?
questions.explanation: ▲ is two stars, so ▲ + ★ is three stars = 12, and ★ = 4. ▲ = 8. 8 − 4 = 4.

distractors.D: gave ▲

questions.skill: Best value
questions.stem: At the pool, a single entry costs $6, a 10-visit pass costs $48 and a monthly pass (unlimited visits for 4 weeks) costs $55. Max wants to swim 3 times a week for 4 weeks. What is the cheapest he can pay?
questions.explanation: Max needs 12 visits. Singles: 12 × $6 = $72. A 10-visit pass plus 2 singles: $48 + $12 = $60. The monthly pass: $55. Cheapest: $55.

distractors.D: 12 single tickets

questions.skill: Weaken: another reason for the result
questions.stem:
Leo says: 'Our class scored higher on the spelling test this term than last term, so the new spelling app must be working.'
Which statement, if true, most weakens Leo's argument?

options.A: This term's spelling test used much easier words than last term's test.
options.B: The app has games as well as spelling lists.
options.C: Leo's class uses the app three times a week.
options.D: Other classes have asked to use the app too.

questions.explanation: If the test was easier, higher scores could be explained by the easier words, not by the app.

distractors.B: describes the app; doesn't challenge the reasoning
distractors.D: popularity doesn't show whether it works

questions.skill: Spot the mistake: "all winners did X" does not mean "everyone who does X wins"
questions.stem:
Noah says: 'Everyone who has won the art prize took lessons from Ms Lee. I take lessons from Ms Lee, so I will win the art prize.'
Which statement shows the mistake Noah has made?

options.A: Ms Lee may not be the best art teacher in the school.
options.B: Noah might not enter the art prize this year.
options.C: Some winners may have had lessons from other teachers as well.
options.D: Many students who take lessons from Ms Lee might not win.

questions.explanation: All winners had lessons from Ms Lee, but that doesn't mean all of Ms Lee's students win. Lots of her students could miss out, and Noah could be one of them.

distractors.A: Noah's mistake isn't about how good Ms Lee is
distractors.B: possible, but not the error in his reasoning

questions.skill: Tracking amounts through several swaps

distractors.B: slip in tracking Ali
distractors.D: forgot Ali received 3

questions.skill: Ages: past and future
questions.stem: Tia's brother is 10 years old. In 4 years' time, Tia will be twice as old as her brother was 2 years ago. How old is Tia now?
questions.explanation: Two years ago her brother was 8. Twice that is 16, which is Tia's age in 4 years. So Tia is 16 − 4 = 12 now.

distractors.D: Tia's age in 4 years, not now

questions.skill: Who owns which pet (elimination)
questions.stem:
Ruby, Sid, Tom and Uma each have a different pet: a cat, a dog, a rabbit or a fish.
• Ruby has either the cat or the fish, and her pet does not purr.
• Sid's pet does not bark and does not swim.
• Tom's pet is not the cat or the rabbit.
• Uma's pet is not the fish or the rabbit.
Who has the dog?
questions.explanation: Ruby has the cat or the fish, and her pet doesn't purr, so Ruby has the fish. Tom can't have the cat or the rabbit, and the fish is taken, so Tom has the dog. (Then Uma can't have the rabbit, so she has the cat, and Sid has the rabbit.)

distractors.B: Ruby has the fish
distractors.D: Uma has the cat

questions.skill: Days of the week after a number of days
questions.stem: The school fete is held 18 days after Monday 1 March. On which day of the week is the fete?
questions.explanation: 18 days = 2 weeks + 4 days. Two weeks after a Monday is a Monday; 4 more days is Friday (19 March).

distractors.D: counted the dates instead of the days

questions.skill: Counting games in a round robin
questions.stem: Five teams are in a netball competition. Each team plays every other team exactly once. How many games are played?
questions.explanation: Team 1 plays 4 games, team 2 plays 3 new games, then 2, then 1: 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10. (5 × 4 = 20 counts each game twice.)

distractors.D: used 5 × 5

questions.skill: What must be true: working backwards from a rule
questions.stem:
Every student who finishes the reading challenge gets a certificate. Every student who gets a certificate is invited to the morning tea. Hana was not invited to the morning tea.
Which statement must be true?

options.A: Hana got a certificate but missed the morning tea.
options.B: Hana did not finish the reading challenge.
options.D: Hana finished the challenge but lost her certificate.

questions.explanation: If Hana had finished, she would have got a certificate, and then she would have been invited. She wasn't invited, so she can't have finished.

distractors.A: a certificate means an invitation, and she had none
distractors.C: we know nothing about her feelings
distractors.D: finishing always leads to an invitation

questions.skill: Identify the hidden assumption
questions.stem:
Ben says: 'I scored 9 goals this season and Sam scored only 6, so I am a better soccer player than Sam.'
Which assumption has Ben made?

options.A: Sam played in every game this season.
options.B: Ben will score more goals than Sam next season too.
options.C: Scoring more goals is what makes someone a better player.
options.D: Their team won most of its games this season.

questions.explanation: Ben jumps from 'more goals' to 'better player'. That only works if goals are what decide who is better, but defenders and goalkeepers can be excellent without scoring.

distractors.A: Ben's argument doesn't need this to be true
distractors.B: about the future, not his reasoning
distractors.D: team results don't link to the comparison

questions.skill: Whose reasoning: a rule tells you nothing outside it
questions.stem:
Information: Whenever it rains on a Saturday, the park market is cancelled.

Ollie: 'The market was cancelled last Saturday, so it must have rained.'
Priya: 'It didn't rain on Sunday, so the market must have gone ahead on Sunday.'

If the information is true, whose reasoning is correct?
questions.explanation: Ollie reverses the rule: rain causes cancellation, but the market could be cancelled for other reasons. Priya uses a rule about Saturdays to decide something about Sunday, and we don't even know the market runs on Sundays.

distractors.B: the rule is only about Saturdays

questions.stem:
Information: To enter the science fair, a project must be checked by a teacher. Every project that wins a prize is put on display in the library.

Sam: 'Jay's project won a prize, so it must have been checked by a teacher.'

If the information is true, whose reasoning is correct?

questions.stem:
Kai, Lea, Max and Nora sit in a row of four seats, numbered 1 to 4 from left to right.
• Kai is not in an end seat.
• Lea sits directly to the right of Kai.
• Max does not sit next to Lea.
• Nora is not in seat 1.
Which seat must Max be in?
questions.explanation:
Kai is in seat 2 or 3, with Lea directly to his right.
• Kai 2, Lea 3: Max can't be in 4 (next to Lea), so Max is in 1 and Nora in 4.
• Kai 3, Lea 4: seats 1 and 2 are left, and Nora can't have seat 1, so Max is in 1 and Nora in 2.

distractors.B: only possible for Nora
distractors.D: Max would be next to Lea in one case, and Nora is there in the other

Which statement must be true?

options.B: Everyone in the choir is in the drama club.
options.C: Some students in the drama club play in the band.
options.D: Everyone in the band is in the choir.

questions.explanation: Some choir students play in the band, and no band player is in drama. So those choir students are definitely not in the drama club.

Zara does one activity each weekday afternoon: swimming, piano, art, soccer and homework club, a different one each day.
• Soccer is the day after swimming.
• Piano is not on Monday or Friday.
• Art is on Wednesday.
• Homework club is earlier in the week than piano.
On which day does Zara play soccer?
questions.explanation: Art is Wednesday. Piano must be Tuesday or Thursday, with homework club earlier. If piano is Thursday, swimming and soccer need two days in a row from Monday, Tuesday and Friday, so Monday and Tuesday, and then homework club would have to be Friday, which is after piano ✗. distractors.B: one of the conditions rules this out
distractors.C: one of the conditions rules this out
